title: Graves above the Ely
place: Monastic burial ground on Llandough hill, above the Ely

cast.A_MARY: a woman of the district at the graveside (prologue, invented)

shots.direction: (~10 s) Date-and-place card over an establishing still. Late autumn afternoon on the crown of Llandough hill. Low grey cloud and wet grass. Below and far off, the River Ely winds through broad reed marshes toward a hazy tidal estuary. The view is inland from a hilltop, with no shoreline at the foot of the hill. A slow push-in. Ambience: wind in the grass, distant curlews over the marsh.

captions.text: c. 650 · Llandough hill, above the Ely

shots.direction: (~14 s) A small funeral procession crosses the hilltop burial ground. Low turf mounds and fresh-cut graves run in rough rows, aligned west to east. Two lay brothers carry a body wrapped in a plain undyed linen shroud on a wooden bier. The monk walks ahead, and the woman follows with her cloak drawn close. In the background stands a small timber church with a thatched roof, with smoke rising from a hut beyond. Slow lateral drift. Ambience: footsteps, low Latin psalm chant under the wind.

Ahead walks a monk in his 40s-70s with a broad weathered face, grey-flecked beard, Insular frontal tonsure, rough undyed wool habit and heavy hands. Behind follows a Welsh woman in her 20s-30s with dark brown hair under a wool head-cloth, strong cheekbones, grey-green eyes, a small mole on her left cheek and a dark wool cloak. A small timber church with a thatched roof stands in the background, with marshland and river far below. Overcast light. No stone ruins shown, no text, no heraldry, invented faces.

shots.direction: (~10 s) Medium close on the monk at the graveside as the shrouded body is lowered, head to the west. He scatters a handful of earth and speaks gently to the dead woman.

lines.accent: South Wales Welsh, low and steady (mark for native review)
lines.cy: Pridd i bridd. Gorwedd di yma gyda'r lleill, a'th wyneb tua'r dwyrain, tua'r wawr.
lines.en: Earth to earth. Lie here with the others, your face to the east, toward the dawn.
lines.es: Tierra a la tierra. Descansá acá con los demás, con la cara hacia el este, hacia el alba.

shots.direction: (~11 s) Close on the woman across the grave. She looks along the rows of mounds stretching away, then back to the monk.
shots.image_prompt: Photoreal 16:9 close-up, early medieval Wales c. 650 AD. A Welsh woman with dark brown hair under a wool head-cloth, strong cheekbones, grey-green eyes, a small mole on her left cheek and a dark wool cloak stands at a graveside, grief held in check. Behind her, rows of low turf grave mounds recede across an inland hilltop. Overcast light. No text, no heraldry, invented face.

lines.accent: South Wales Welsh, quiet (mark for native review)
lines.cy: Mae cymaint ohonyn nhw, frawd. Rhes ar ôl rhes. Bob gaeaf, mwy. Fydd hi'n unig yma?
lines.en: There are so many of them, brother. Row after row. Every winter, more. Will she be lonely here?
lines.es: Son tantos, hermano. Fila tras fila. Cada invierno, más. ¿Va a estar sola acá?

shots.direction: (~15 s) The monk turns slightly and nods toward the little thatched timber church behind them as he answers her.
shots.image_prompt: Photoreal 16:9 medium shot, early medieval Wales c. 650 AD. A monk with a grey-flecked beard, Insular frontal tonsure and undyed wool habit turns toward a small thatched timber church on a grassy hilltop and gestures gently with one hand. Grave mounds lie around him under a soft overcast sky. No stone ruins, no text, no heraldry, invented face.

lines.accent: South Wales Welsh, warm (mark for native review)
lines.cy: Unig? Byth. Mae'r brodyr yn canu'r salmau yma bob cyfnos, uwchben yr Elái. Roedd yr eglwys fach hon yn hen pan ddes i, a bydd hi yma ar ôl i ni fynd.
lines.en: Lonely? Never. The brothers sing the psalms here every dusk, above the Ely. This little church was old when I came, and it will be here after we are gone.
lines.es: ¿Sola? Nunca. Los hermanos cantan los salmos acá todos los atardeceres, sobre el Ely. Esta iglesita ya era vieja cuando llegué, y va a seguir acá cuando nos hayamos ido.

shots.direction: (~9 s) Close on the woman as a lay brother's wooden spade strikes something hard at the edge of the grave with a dull knock. She glances down at the spoil heap, where a squared, weathered stone fragment shows in the soil, then looks back up.
shots.image_prompt: Photoreal 16:9 close-up, early medieval Wales c. 650 AD. A Welsh woman with dark brown hair under a wool head-cloth, grey-green eyes and a small mole on her left cheek glances down at a heap of fresh grave soil. A single small weathered squared stone fragment lies half-buried in the earth beside a wooden spade. Overcast light. No buildings or ruins visible, no text, no heraldry, invented face.

lines.accent: South Wales Welsh (mark for native review)
lines.cy: A dan y dywarchen, yr hen gerrig. Mae'r rhawiau'n eu taro nhw o hyd.
lines.en: And under the turf, the old stones. The spades still strike them.
lines.es: Y bajo el pasto, las piedras viejas. Las palas siguen dando con ellas.

shots.direction: (~11 s) The monk looks at the stone fragment without concern, then offers the woman his hand to lead her from the grave as the lay brothers begin to fill it.
shots.image_prompt: Photoreal 16:9 medium shot, early medieval Wales c. 650 AD. A monk with a grey-flecked beard, Insular frontal tonsure and undyed wool habit extends a heavy hand toward a cloaked woman beside a half-filled grave on an inland grassy hilltop. Behind them, two men in wool tunics shovel earth. The light is fading toward dusk. No ruins shown, no text, no heraldry, invented faces.

lines.accent: South Wales Welsh, gentle (mark for native review)
lines.cy: Cerrig y Rhufeiniaid ydyn nhw. Maen nhw wedi hen fynd; ni sy'n aros. Dere. Mae'r brodyr yn disgwyl amdanon ni.
lines.en: They are the Romans' stones. They are long gone; we are the ones who stay. Come. The brothers are waiting for us.
lines.es: Son piedras de los romanos. Ellos se fueron hace mucho; nosotros somos los que quedamos. Vení. Los hermanos nos esperan.

shots.direction: (~16 s) Wide closing still at dusk. The monk and the woman walk toward the small thatched church, where a faint light shows in the doorway. The new mound joins the rows on the hill, and the Ely marshes lie dim and silver below. Slow pull-back. Ambience: psalm chant rising from the church, wind, a last curlew.
